content.value_statement: Regulated data projects often fail when generic assetization methods overlook industry rules. This skill structures compliance-first assessments for carbon, seed, energy, and public data.
actual_capabilities: Identifies sector-specific compliance gates for carbon, seed, energy storage, and public data projects.
Maps data characteristics, ownership concerns, value scenarios, and likely buyer structures.
Separates official regulatory mechanisms from commercial RWA structures and claims.
Produces staged feasibility assessments, deliverable lists, quality checks, and risk warnings.
Routes questions to defined specialist roles and combines their conclusions into one assessment.
Compares assetization paths such as accounting recognition, structured rights, and authorized public-data operation.
limitations: The knowledge base reflects a stated review date and may not include later policy changes.
The skill does not replace legal, accounting, valuation, cybersecurity, or regulatory advice.
It does not verify user evidence, obtain approvals, or submit materials to authorities.
Financial ranges and commercialization paths require independent validation with current market data.

use_cases.title: Screen a Carbon Data Project
use_cases.description: Assess MRV readiness, CCER boundaries, evidence gaps, and possible assetization paths before commissioning specialist work.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Energy Data Commercialization
use_cases.description: Classify storage or charging data, identify CII and important-data concerns, and test whether cash flows are measurable.

use_cases.title: Plan Public Data Authorization
use_cases.description: Structure the authorization process, required deliverables, term controls, operating boundaries, and renewal reminders for a regional project.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Industry Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this [industry] data project. List its data types, main compliance gates, missing evidence, and the next three actions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner assessment of an early project idea

prompt_templates.title: Compare Assetization Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare accounting recognition, data licensing, authorized operation, and structured revenue rights for [project]. Explain eligibility, blockers, evidence, and tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate selection of a commercialization route

prompt_templates.title: Build a Cross-Role Delivery Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased delivery plan for [project]. Assign specialist responsibilities, required inputs, deliverables, quality checks, decision gates, and escalation points.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a multidisciplinary team

prompt_templates.title: Challenge an Investment Proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Stress-test this [industry] data investment proposal. Separate verified facts from assumptions, test regulatory claims, assess measurable cash flows, and recommend proceed, pause, or reject.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before investment or executive approval

output_examples.input: Can charging-network usage data support an assetization project?
output_examples.output: Conditional feasibility. First classify personal, operational, and grid-related data. Confirm de-identification, CII exposure, ownership, auditability, and measurable revenue before selecting a structure.

output_examples.input: How should a city plan a five-year public-data authorization?
output_examples.output: Use the five-step authorization process and document scope, operator selection, security duties, product boundaries, and revenue allocation. Track the shorter registration renewal separately.

output_examples.input: Can verified emissions reductions be marketed as official carbon credits?
output_examples.output: Not automatically. Verify the approved methodology, MRV evidence, validation path, crediting period, registration status, and issuance estimate. Keep commercial carbon claims distinct from official CCER.

best_practices: Provide the jurisdiction, project stage, data inventory, participants, intended buyers, and available evidence.
Confirm current policies with official sources before relying on dates, limits, or approval requirements.
Keep regulatory rights, data rights, intellectual property, and revenue rights separate throughout the assessment.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a generic data assetization process as sufficient for a regulated industry.
Do not present commercial tokens, revenue rights, or private certificates as official regulatory instruments.
Do not infer ownership, approval, or financial value when supporting evidence is missing.

faq.question: Which industries does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers carbon, seed, power and energy storage, and public data authorization scenarios.

faq.question: Does it provide legal or regulatory approval?
faq.answer: No. It organizes issues and evidence but does not replace qualified advisers or competent authorities.

faq.question: Can it calculate a final data asset valuation?
faq.answer: No. It can identify valuation inputs and cash-flow questions, but specialists must validate assumptions and issue formal opinions.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the jurisdiction, data inventory, participants, project stage, proposed transaction, available approvals, and supporting evidence.

faq.question: Can it compare several industries?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare compliance gates, ownership complexity, buyers, commercialization routes, and required deliverables across the four covered sectors.

faq.question: How current is the regulatory guidance?
faq.answer: The source states a review date of September 23, 2026. Verify every policy and deadline against current official publications.
